candidates.title: Low Back Pain & Low Back Extensions
candidates.description:
Low Back Pain and Low Back Extensions 

Low Back Extensions on a 45-degree bench have to be one of the most common exercises I see for people trying to improve their low back.

Problem is, a lot of people who have low back pain complain about how this exercise makes things worse.

And while there isn't fundamentally anything wrong with the exercise, the common fault I see from those with back pain stem from this very important concept.

Cold Water Back — This is an analogy I use with all my clients to help fix their posture immediately.

Imagine cold water running down your back; your natural reaction is to tense up and retract your scapulas — this movement, even if it's exaggerated, when you go to hip hinge or perform extensions really has the ability to bulletproof your low back.

And if you have a bad low back, chances are, this fundamental cue is missing in your training.

The second element is to work on full body posterior extension with exercises like this "Back Plank."

Unlike the low back extension where the top side of your body is free to move, the back plank teaches you to contract all the muscles in sync (the glutes, hamstrings, low back) to maintain a nice solid line.

And the pressure from the bench or the Swiss ball forces you to push against it utilizing your upper back and ultimately helps you reinforce good “cold water” mechanics.

If you're experiencing low back pain and haven't addressed these fundamental issues first, doing low back extensions won't help you improve—it may even make things worse.
